title: Immunoprecipitation, Decross-linking, and DNA Extraction
author: Vasso Makrantoni
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bn3xmgpn
materials: Perform data analysis using Microsoft Excel software using the following formulas: Determine the ChIP enrichment (i.e., ChIP/Input value), by calculating ΔCt using the following formula: ΔCt = Ct^{ChIP} − (Ct^{Input} − log_{primer efficiency} (Input dilution factor)) From this, the ChIP enrichment is calculated using: ChIP/Input = (primer efficiency)^{(−ΔCt)} where Ct values are mean threshold cycles of PCR performed in triplicate per DNA sample. To increase accuracy and reproducibility, we advise the use of an electronic dispensing pipette for qPCR. For primer design we recommend the use of Prime3Plus software. In the general settings of the software, we use product size range 70–200 bp (optimal amplicon size ~120 bp), optimal primer size 20 bp in length and optimal primer Tm for use with Luna Universal Probe qPCR Master Mix should be designed to anneal at 60 °C, with optimal primer GC% between 50% and 60%. Once primers are designed determine their efficiency and specificity using genomic DNA prior to performing qPCR with ChIP DNA sample. Finally, also include a No Template Control (NTC) in the reaction, where no amplification and no melting curve should be generated.

steps.title: Prewash Protein G Dynabeads
steps.instruction: Prewash (n × 15 µL) Protein G Dynabeads per IP sample in 1 mL ice‑cold 1× FA buffer (0.1 % SDS, 1 mM PMSF, protease inhibitors) with rotation for 5 min, place tubes on a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Add antibody and bind chromatin
steps.instruction: To each 1 mL chromatin extract add the specified antibody (e.g., 10 µL 9E10, 7.5 µL 12CA5, 10 µL SV5‑PK1, 10 µL anti‑GFP, 5 µL M2 FLAG) and 15 µL pre‑washed Dynabeads, mix; optionally reduce SDS to a final 0.05 % in 2×FA buffer. No blocking or pre‑clearing is required.

steps.title: Incubate immunoprecipitation overnight
steps.instruction: Rotate the tubes on a wheel at 4 °C for ~16 h (overnight) to allow antibody‑chromatin binding.

steps.title: Wash immunoprecipitated beads
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnetic rack, discard supernatant, then sequentially wash beads with 1 mL of each ChIP Wash buffer (1 = low salt, 2 = high salt, 3, 4) while rotating for 5 min at room temperature; discard supernatant after each wash.

substeps.instruction: Wash with 1 mL ChIP Wash buffer 1 (low salt), rotate 5 min, RT, discard supernatant.
Wash with 1 mL ChIP Wash buffer 2 (high salt), rotate 5 min, RT, discard supernatant.
Wash with 1 mL ChIP Wash buffer 3, rotate 5 min, RT, discard supernatant.
Wash with 1 mL ChIP Wash buffer 4, rotate 5 min, RT, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Collect beads after final wash
steps.instruction: After the last wash, place the tubes on a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Add Chelex‑100 resin slurry
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 10 % (w/v) Chelex‑100 slurry in sterile water to each IP sample (beads) and to each 10 µL thawed Input sample; keep the Chelex beads suspended while pipetting.

steps.title: Vortex and boil samples
steps.instruction: Briefly vortex the tubes to mix the Chelex slurry, then boil for 10 min.

steps.title: Cool and centrifuge samples
steps.instruction: Cool the tubes to room temperature, then centrifuge briefly at 400 × g to collect condensate at the bottom of the tube; proceed immediately to the next step.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Add 2.5 µL Proteinase K (10 mg mL⁻¹) to each sample and incubate at 55 °C for 30 min on a heat block, mixing occasionally to resuspend the beads.

steps.title: Inactivate Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Boil the samples at 100 °C for 10 min to inactivate Proteinase K.

steps.title: Collect DNA supernatant
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes briefly at 400 × g, then carefully transfer ~120 µL of the DNA‑containing supernatant to a new tube, avoiding any Chelex resin.

steps.title: Store DNA at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Store the collected DNA samples at –20 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Set up qPCR reaction
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 µL qPCR reactions with Luna Universal Probe qPCR Master Mix: 3 µL DNA template (Input diluted 1:300, IP diluted 1:6), 0.125 µL primer pair (20 µM each), 5 µL master mix, add nuclease‑free water to 10 µL total; run the recommended program.

steps.title: Quantify DNA for library preparation
steps.instruction: Measure 3 µL of each ChIP product and Input sample using the Qubit HS kit; typical yields are 2–10 ng.

steps.title: Pool beads and resuspend in TES
steps.instruction: Pool magnetic beads from identical IP samples together and resuspend the combined beads in 200 µL TES buffer.

steps.title: Elute chromatin from beads
steps.instruction: Incubate the resuspended beads in TES buffer at 65 °C for 15 min to elute the immunoprecipitated chromatin.

steps.title: Transfer eluted DNA to LoBind tube
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a magnetic rack, then transfer the supernatant (the IP DNA) to a new LoBind DNA tube.

steps.title: Dilute Input sample with TES
steps.instruction: Add 190 µL TES buffer to 10 µL pooled Input sample in a LoBind DNA tube.

steps.title: Decross‑link samples overnight
steps.instruction: Incubate both IP and Input samples at 65 °C for at least 6 h (overnight) to reverse cross‑links.

steps.title: RNase treatment of samples
steps.instruction: Cool the samples, add 2 µL RNase (10 mg mL⁻¹) and incubate for 1 h at 37 °C to degrade RNA.

steps.title: Second Proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K (10 mg mL⁻¹) per 200 µL sample and incubate at 65 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Purify library
steps.instruction: Purify the ChIP‑seq library using the Wizard SV purification kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Quantify DNA after purification
steps.instruction: Again quantify 3 µL of the purified ChIP‑seq library and Input using the Qubit HS kit; typical yields remain 2–10 ng.
